input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for (and paid for by) Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails even the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables. The rest of the IP architecture already sits at our preferred position: Customer owns Customer Data with Vendor's rights limited to processing it to provide, secure, support and improve the Services (14.1); Vendor retains Vendor Technology, defined as its pre-existing technology (14.3, 1.8); Customer has a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable (13.2, 14.3); and no joint ownership arises absent a signed instrument setting out exploitation rights (14.4). The shortest complete cure is therefore to reverse 14.2 to Customer ownership with an express assignment, which leaves 13.2, 14.3 and 10.1 intact.

mappings.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
mappings.quote: For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence

mappings.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
mappings.quote: Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence

mappings.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
mappings.quote: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business

mappings.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
mappings.quote: As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services.

mappings.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
mappings.quote: No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

mappings.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
mappings.quote: No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights.

proposal.summary: Customer owns Deliverables; Vendor assigns them
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must own the Deliverables we pay for, so we have reversed Section 14.2 to give Customer ownership with an assignment from Vendor; Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 and Customer's perpetual licence to embedded Vendor Technology under Section 13.2 is unchanged.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.
